text: ῥυπαρεύομαι, I am filthy; hence (morally), I am stained with sin.
ῥυπαρία, defilement.
ῥυπαρός, shabby, soiled: hence morally, filthy, corrupt, sinful, Rev. xxii 11.
ῥύπος, filth, dirt.
ῥύσις, flowing; ῥύσις αἵματος, hemorrhage.
ῥυτίς, a wrinkle of age.
Ῥωμαϊστί, in the Latin language.
Ῥώμη, Rome, the famous city on the Tiber, the capital of the Roman Empire.
gloss: Rome, the famous city on the Tiber

text: ῥώννυμι, I make strong: perf. mid. imperative, a formula of correspondence, at the end of a letter, ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε (uale, ualete), farewell.
σαβαχθανεί (Aramaic), thou hast forsaken.
σαβαώθ (Hebrew), hosts, armies.
σαββατισμός, a resting as on the sabbath.
gloss: a resting as on the sabbath

text: σαγήνη, a fishing-net.
Σαδώκ (Hebr.), Zadok, an ancestor of Jesus.
σαίνω (properly of dogs, I wag the tail, fawn: then met. I fawn upon, beguile), I draw aside, allure from the right path: perhaps the v. l. σιαίνεσθαι, to be disturbed (troubled), ought to be read.
gloss: I draw aside, allure from the right path

text: σάκκος (a Semitic word), sackcloth, sacking, a rough mourning dress held together by string, and hanging on the bare body.
Σαλά (Hebr.), Sala, the name of two of the ancestors of Jesus (v. l. in Lk. iii 32).
gloss: Sala, the name of two of the ancestors of Jesus

text: Σαλαθιήλ (Hebr.), Salathiel, son of Jechonias and father (according to one tradition) of Zerubbabel.
Σαλαμίς, Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus.
gloss: Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus

text: Σαλείμ, Salim, a place eight Roman miles south of Scythopolis in the extreme north of Samaria.
gloss: Salim, a place eight Roman miles south of Scythopolis

text: Σαλήμ, Salem, doubtless identical with Jerusalem.
Σαλμών, Salmon, son of Naasson and father of Boes (Boaz) (v. l. in Lk. iii 32).
gloss: Salmon, son of Naasson and father of Boes (Boaz)

text: Σαλμώνη, Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete.
gloss: Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete

text: σάλος, a rough sea, surf.
σαλπιστής, a bugler, trumpeter.
Σαλώμη, Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John, the disciples.
gloss: Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John

text: Σαμαρείτης, a Samaritan, an inhabitant of Samaria.
gloss: a Samaritan, an inhabitant of Samaria

text: Σαμαρεῖτις, a Samaritan woman.
Σαμοθρᾴκη, Samothrace, an island south of the province of Thrace.
gloss: Samothrace, an island south of the province of Thrace

text: Σάμος, Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor, near Ephesus and Miletus.
gloss: Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor

text: Σαμουήλ (Hebr.), Samuhel, Samuel, an Old Testament prophet.
gloss: Samuhel, Samuel, an Old Testament prophet

text: Σαμψών (Hebr.), Sampson, Samson, one of the Judges of Israel.
gloss: Sampson, Samson, one of the Judges of Israel

text: σανδάλιον, a sandal, an open-work shoe, a shoe.
gloss: a sandal, an open-work shoe, a shoe

text: σανίς, a plank, board.
Σαούλ, (a) Saul, the first king of Israel, Ac. xiii 21; (b) Saul, the Hebrew name of the Apostle to the Gentiles (see Σαῦλος).
gloss: Saul, the first king of Israel

text: σαπρός (puter), crumbling, decayed, decaying, rotten; hence, old and worn out, stale, worthless: met. corrupt, Eph. iv 29.
Σάπφειρα (perhaps from an Aramaic word meaning beautiful), Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian.
gloss: Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian

text: σάπφειρος (Semitic), a sapphire; lapis lazuli.
σαργάνη, a mat-basket, a large basket of flexible material closed by sewing and usually employed to hold slices of salt fish (raisins and figs are also mentioned).
gloss: a mat-basket, a large basket of flexible material

text: Σάρδεις, Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia.
gloss: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia

text: σάρδιον, sardius, sard, a quartz of a deep red colour.
gloss: sardius, sard, a quartz of a deep red colour

text: σαρδόνυξ, sardonyx.
Σάρεπτα, Sarepta, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia.
gloss: Sarepta, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia

text: σαρκικός (carnalis), generally ethical, belonging to σάρξ (which see), belonging to the natural life of man as a creature of flesh, with the characteristics of σάρξ, fleshly, unspiritual, carnal.
σάρκινος (carneus), material, made of flesh, consisting of flesh.
gloss: material, made of flesh, consisting of flesh

text: σαρόω, I sweep.
Σάρρα (Hebr.), Sarah, wife of Abraham.
Σαρών, Sharon, the maritime plain between Carmel and Joppa.
gloss: Sharon, the maritime plain between Carmel and Joppa

text: σάτον (Aramaic), a large measure equivalent to 1½ modii, that is, nearly three English gallons.
gloss: a large measure equivalent to 1½ modii

text: σβέννυμι, ζβέννυμι, I extinguish, put out: met. 1 Thess. v 19.
σεβάζομαι, I reverence, worship.
σέβασμα, an object of worship, a thing worshipped.
gloss: an object of worship, a thing worshipped

text: Σεβαστός (official Greek equivalent of Augustus), Augustus, the name meaning ‘worthy to be reverenced (worshipped)’, given to Octavian by the Senate in Jan. 27 B.C., and retained by most of his successors, e.g. by Nero, to whom it refers in Ac. xxv 21, 25, where it is of course used by non-Christians: in Ac. xxvii 1 σπεῖρα Σεβαστή is the official equivalent of a cohors Augusta (a cohors I Augusta had its headquarters in Batanaea in NE. Palestine).
σειρός (properly a pit, excavation for the storage of grain), a pit: v. l. σειρά, a chain, fetter.
note: Headword printed is σειρός; σειρά appears in it as v. l. Gloss taken from Souter's meaning for σειρά.

text: σείω, I shake.
Σέκουνδος (Latin), Secundus, a Christian of Thessalonica.
Σελεύκεια, Seleucia, on the Syrian coast, the harbour of Syrian Antioch.
σελήνη, the moon.
σεληνιάζω, I bring under the influence of the moon: pass. I am epileptic (the state of an epileptic being attributed to the moon [σελήνη]).
gloss: I bring under the influence of the moon

text: Σεμεείν (Hebr.), Semein, an ancestor of Jesus.
σεμίδαλις, the finest wheaten meal.
σεμνός (grauis), grave, worthy of respect.
σεμνότης (grauitas), gravity, dignified behaviour.
Σέργιος, Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus.
gloss: Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus

text: Σερούχ (Hebr.), Seruch, an ancestor of Jesus.
Σήθ (Hebr.), Seth, third son of Adam.
Σήμ (Hebr.), Shem, a son of Noah.
σημαίνω (a technical term for the speech of a communicator of an oracle), I indicate by a word; I point out in a letter (by letter), Ac. xxv 27.
σημειόομαι, I mark (notify) for myself; hence, with an idea of disapprobation added.
σήπω, tr. I cause to rot: 2 perf. σέσηπα, I have rotted, I am rotten.
σής, a moth.
σητόβρωτος, moth-eaten.
σθενόω, I strengthen.
σιαγών, a cheek.
σιγάω, I am silent.
σιγή, silence.
σίδηρος, iron.
Σιδών, Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia: in Mk. vii 31 perhaps an error for Saidan = Bethsaida.
gloss: Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia

text: Σιδώνιος, belonging to Sidon, Sidonian; hence, as subst., a Sidonian: ἡ Σιδωνία (sc. χώρα), the region or territory of Sidon, Lk. iv 26.
σικάριος (Latin, from sica, a stiletto), an assassin, a murderer; with reference to a fanatical Jewish political faction, accustomed to assassinate their opponents.
σίκερα (Aramaic), an intoxicating drink, a strong fruit-wine.
gloss: an intoxicating drink, a strong fruit-wine
note: fruit-wine is split at a line end; hyphen kept as a real compound hyphen.

text: Σίλας (Western documents spell Σιλέας), Silas, a Jewish prophet and evangelist, a Roman citizen and a helper of St. Paul. The name is generally regarded as a pet-form (used in Ac. only) of Σιλουανός, and Silas is in consequence identified with him.
gloss: Silas, a Jewish prophet and evangelist
note: pet-form is split at a line end; hyphen kept as a real compound hyphen.

text: Σιλουανός (Latin, Siluanus) Silvanus: see Σίλας.
note: This target's current_text is a fragment of the Σίλας entry (4707), split at the word Σιλουανός inside it; it is not a separate entry. The only Σιλουανός entry on the page is entry 4709 (text repeated here). Likely a duplicate to drop.

text: Σιλουανός (Latin, Siluanus) Silvanus: see Σίλας.
Σιλωάμ, Siloam, Shiloah, a spring (the only spring) within the walls, in the SE. corner of Jerusalem. The name is Aramaic and really a substantive (= discharge or gushing forth of water).
gloss: Siloam, Shiloah, a spring (the only spring) within the walls

text: σιμικίνθιον (Latin, semicinctium), an artisan’s working-apron.
note: working-apron is split at a line end; hyphen kept as a real compound hyphen.

text: Σινά, Sinai, a mountain in Arabia: according to Hebrew allegorical methods of interpretation identified with Hagar, concubine of Abraham, Gal. iv 25 (Arabic hadjar = rock, stone, and thus comes the equation Hagar = Sinai).
σίναπι, mustard.

σινδών (Semitic), a fine light dress worn over the underclothing, or a nightgown, or a sheet hastily seized, Mk. xiv 51: of the grave-clothes of Jesus, probably a piece of unused linen, Mk. xv 46, &c.
gloss: a fine light dress worn over the underclothing

text: σινιάζω, I sift, winnow.
σιρικός (an inexact spelling of σηρικός, adj. formed from Σῆρες, the Chinese, from whose country silk was obtained), silken; silk fabrics (or garments).
σιτευτός (altilis), fed up (with grain), fattened.
σιτίον, food made of corn, bread.
σιτιστός, the same in meaning as the much commoner σιτευτός.
gloss: the same in meaning as the much commoner σιτευτός

text: σιτομέτριον, measure of corn, portion of corn, allowance of corn.
gloss: measure of corn, portion of corn, allowance of corn

text: Σιών, Sion, Zion, the mountain on which the Davidic citadel of Jerusalem was built, and thus the centre of the life of the people Israel.
σκάπτω, I dig.
σκάφη, a small boat, towed behind.
σκέλος, a leg.
σκέπασμα, strictly roofing, shelter, but with special reference to clothing.
Σκευᾶς, Sceva, an inhabitant of Ephesus.
σκευή (a collective noun), tackle.

σκηνοπηγία, sometimes called ἑορτὴ [τῶν] σκηνῶν or ἑορτὴ [τῆς] σκηνοπηγίας, the Feast of Tabernacles (lit. of booth-building), the great festival of the Jews, held in October, originally the Feast of Ingathering.
σκηνοποιός, a tentmaker.
σκῆνος, a tent: so met. (used in Pythagorean philosophy) of the body as the temporary dwelling-place of the soul.
σκήνωμα, a tent, really a humble word for the permanent building aimed at, Ac. vii 46: of the body as the temporary abode of the soul.
σκιρτάω, I leap, bound, jump.
σκληροκαρδία (Hebraistic, from σκληρός and καρδία, as the seat of the will), stiffness, stubbornness, unyieldingness, obduracy.
σκληρός (properly hard), (a) strong, James iii 4; (b) met. harsh, rough; almost = dangerous, Ac. xxvi 14.
σκληρότης, obstinacy.
σκληροτράχηλος, stiff-necked, stubborn.
σκληρύνω, I make unyielding.
σκολιός, crooked: hence met. perverse, of turning off from the truth, crooked in nature.
σκόλοψ, originally a stake; but commonly in N.T. times a thorn; a splinter: met. referring to some physical trouble.
σκοπέω, I look upon, I gaze upon, watch.
gloss: I look upon, I gaze upon, watch

text: σκοπός, a mark to be aimed at (e.g. by an archer).
gloss: a mark to be aimed at

text: σκορπίζω, I scatter.
σκορπίος, a scorpion.
σκοτεινός, dark.
σκοτόω, I darken, lit. or met.
note: The target's current_text was the σκοτίζω entry; transcribed the σκοτόω entry, which is the one for this lemma.

text: σκύβαλον, sweepings, refuse, especially dirt, dung (popularly used of the human skeleton).
Σκύθης, a Scythian, an uncivilized inhabitant of NE. Europe.
gloss: a Scythian, an uncivilized inhabitant of NE. Europe

text: σκυθρωπός, with downcast countenance; sad-faced; gloomy.
σκύλλω (originally, I flay, skin), (a) I tire out by hunting; I distress, Mt. ix 36; (b) (a slang usage in origin) I worry, trouble.
σκωληκόβρωτος, eaten by worms (the word scolex is still used for the tape-worm at one stage of its growth).
σμαράγδινος (ζμαράγδινος), of an emerald.
σμάραγδος (ζμάραγδος), an emerald.
σμύρνα (= μύρρα), myrrh, a fragrant gum-resin from the Arabian Balsamodendron Myrrhae.
Σμύρνα (better spelling Ζμύρνα), Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia.
gloss: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia

text: σμυρνίζω, I spice with myrrh.
Σόδομα, Sodom, a city submerged by the Dead Sea.
gloss: Sodom, a city submerged by the Dead Sea

text: Σολομών (oldest form Σαλωμών, next oldest Σαλομών), Solomon, son of David, King of Israel, and Bathsheba.
gloss: Solomon, son of David, King of Israel

text: σορός, a bier.
σουδάριον (Latin, borrowed by Greek, and thence by Aramaic), a handkerchief.
Σουσάννα, Susannah, a woman of the retinue of Jesus.
gloss: Susannah, a woman of the retinue of Jesus

text: σοφίζω, I make wise: σεσοφισμένος, fictitious, 2 Pet. i 16.
Σπανία (Latin = Hispania), Spain, roughly co-extensive with the modern country of the name.
gloss: Spain, roughly co-extensive with the modern country

text: σπάομαι, I draw my (sword).
σπαράσσω, I throw on the ground.
σπαργανόω, I swathe.
σπαταλάω, I am a voluptuary, I am wanton.
gloss: I am a voluptuary, I am wanton

text: σπεῖρα, a cohort, that is about 600 infantry, under the command of a tribune.
gloss: a cohort, that is about 600 infantry

text: σπεκουλάτωρ (Latin), a scout; a courier: also an executioner.
σπένδω, I pour out an offering of wine to a god: hence pass. met. of the outpouring of one’s life blood in service and suffering.
gloss: I pour out an offering of wine to a god

text: σπερμολόγος (from σπέρμα and λέγω: a slang term in Ac.), used properly of a bird picking up seeds; hence a parasite, hanger on: also of one who picks up scraps of information and retails them at secondhand, an ignorant plagiarist.
gloss: used properly of a bird picking up seeds

text: σπεύδω, I hasten, hurry.
σπήλαιον, a cave (especially as inhabited).
σπιλάς, adjectivally used with ἄνεμος understood, a dirty, foul (lit.), miry wind, perhaps of its effect on the water.
σπίλος, a spot of disfigurement.
σπιλόω, I stain, lit. or met.
σπόγγος, a sponge.
σποδός, ashes.
σπορά, quasi-collective, seed.
σπόριμος, sown: hence τὰ σπόριμα, the crops.
σπόρος, seed.
